mutants.description: Lookahead: the doubling bet is placed only when its outcome is known to win, so ruin never occurs.
Stopping not capped at the horizon: a cap above N is accepted, so the bounded optional-stopping hypothesis drops.
Doob's inequality with the second power: the bound uses E[X_N^2] in place of E[X_N].
Capital ignored: a bet larger than the wealth on hand is accepted, so wealth goes negative after ruin.
Ruin not counted: the expected final wealth is taken over the winning paths only.
Floor instead of half-up rounding of the expected cents, a one-cent error on some seeds.
Doob's maximum taken over k up to N-1 (horizon off by one).
Dyadic conditional expectation uses the cell's left endpoint instead of the midpoint.
Win probability hard-coded to 1/2, so the biased control passes the martingale test.
A hard-coded answer for seed 0: the doubling outcome returns a fixed table when the seed is 0.
Strict affordability: a bet is placed only if its stake is strictly less than the wealth on hand.
Doob's maximum taken with a strict exceedance, so a path that reaches the level exactly is not counted.
Python's built-in round() on the exact expectation, which rounds half to even, so one half cent rounds down.
Dyadic value without the clamp to the last cell, so x = 1 is assigned to a non-existent cell beyond [1 - 2^-n, 1].
Stopping rule that runs to the horizon N instead of the stopping cap, so the stopped walk ignores the cap.
Ruin probability counts one bet too few, so the ruin branch has the wrong probability.
Doob's probability taken at the horizon only, P(|S_N| >= lam), instead of the maximum over every k up to N.
Wealth on a win taken as the capital plus the last stake placed, instead of the capital plus the base stake.
Stopped-walk probability converted to float, so the control walk's expectation is no longer exact.
Doob's bound divided in floating point, E|S_N| / float(lam), so the bound is not an exact Fraction.
Negative stopping level: the walk is never stopped at a level below the start, so the stopped walk runs to the cap.
Horizon check off by one for negatives: a horizon of -1 is accepted by the stopped expectation and returns 0.
Cap check off by one: a stopping cap equal to the horizon N is rejected, though it is bounded by N.
Doob level check off by one: a level of zero is accepted and the probability of reaching it is returned.
Doob horizon check missing for negatives: a horizon of -1 is accepted and returns the empty maximum.
Stake check uses >= : a first stake equal to the capital is rejected, though it is allowed.
Capital check too strict: a capital of exactly one cent is rejected, though it is positive.
Ceiling instead of half-up rounding of the expected cents, so an expectation of 2/5 cent gives one cent.
Dyadic cell tie: a point exactly on a cell's left edge is assigned to the cell on its left.
Stopped walk off by one: the walk takes one step fewer than the stopping cap before it stops.
Stopped walk: paths that never reach the level count as 0 instead of the walk's value at the cap.
Stopping test written as at-or-below the level, so a level of +2 fires at the first step up to +1.
Doob's maximum taken over the signed walk, so excursions below zero are never counted in the probability.
Wealth after ruin taken as capital minus the last stake, instead of minus the sum of all the stakes lost.
Dyadic error divided once more by the number of cells, so each cell's integral is weighted by 2**-n twice.
Probabilities rounded to six decimals before the expected wealth is formed, not once at the end.
Up-step probability read as the down-step probability: the walk's win probability is 1 - p, so the control walk is mirrored.
Wealth after ruin subtracts the stake of the first bet that was not placed, so the ruin wealth is one stake too low.
Dyadic error uses the absolute deviation |M_n - Y| in place of its square, so E|M_n - Y| is returned as the squared error.
Expected cents formed in floats and truncated after adding one half, so the exact value is lost before the rounding.
A stopping level below the start is compared as its absolute value, so a level of -2 fires at +2 instead of -2.
A stopping level equal to the start is treated as reached at time 0, so the stopped value is 0 before any step.
The bet count uses a strict inequality, so a stake that exactly equals the wealth on hand is never placed.
The expected cents are formed as a float before the half-up rounding, so an exact half-cent below the half is lost.
After a win the wealth is taken as the capital alone, without the stake that the win pays.
The probability that every placed bet loses is computed with the win probability p instead of 1 - p.
The stopped walk gives a down step the weight p, not 1 - p, so the weights do not sum to 1 on a biased coin.
The stopping rule is ignored: the expectation is the walk's value at the cap, even on paths that reached the level.
The dyadic error integrates the squared deviation from the cell's left endpoint, not from its midpoint.
The dyadic value at x = 1 is computed from an index one past the last cell, so it is the midpoint of a cell that does not exist.
The stopping rule is checked for one step fewer than its cap, so every path is stopped one step early.
Doob's event uses a strict threshold, so a path that reaches the level exactly is not counted as reaching it.
